en: Jātaka:
The Sixth Book, Chapter on the Unobstructed (Avāriyavagga)
9. The Dhammadhaja Jātaka “Practice the Dhamma, kinsmen;
practice the Dhamma, may it be well with you.”
One who lives according to the Dhamma sleeps happily, both in this world and in the next.
"Truly fortunate is this bird! [he thought].
He spoke as one most righteous in Dhamma;
standing on one foot,
he taught only the Dhamma.
“Do not judge his virtue;
do not praise him without knowing it.
Having eaten both the egg and the chick, [you will know].”
"He speaks of 'Dhamma,
Dhamma,' yet he says one thing with his speech and does another with his body."
Neither in speech nor in body is he established in that Dhamma;
though gentle in speech, his mind is impenetrable.
Channa is like a black snake in a well;
a man bearing the banner of the Dhamma is a saintly person in villages and towns,
difficult for a foolish man to recognize.
Harm this one with your beaks and wings;
harm this one with your feet;
destroy this corpse!
"This one is not worthy of living together.
Thus ends the ninth Jātaka, the Dhammadhaja-jātaka.
